intro_html: New Mexican green chili is all about that tangy, roasted pepper kick, and the slow cooker makes it effortless. Served over rice with 55 grams of protein a bowl, it comes in at about $4.04 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings means a big pot of chili ready to spoon out all week long.
cost_closing_html: About $4.04 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Every serving comes in around 558 calories with 55 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Tangy, warming, and easy on the wallet. Ladle it over rice and you are set. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Canned diced green chiles give you all the roasted pepper flavor without any roasting or peeling. Stock up when they go on sale.
A jar of salsa verde rounds out the sauce so you do not need extra spices. One jar covers the whole batch.
Pork loin keeps this cheap. At about $2 a pound it is the reason this bowl stays easy on the budget.
make_it: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker with the chopped onion.
Pour in the diced green chiles and salsa verde.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it through the green chili sauce.
Let it simmer uncovered for a few minutes if you want the sauce a little thicker.
Serve over cooked white rice and divide into containers.
